<SUMMARY>During the week of May 15-22, the United States President Trump administration committed $2 billion to quantum computing firms, triggering a surge in quantum stocks. China announced new controls and accelerated the development of strategic mineral reserves. Concurrently, a Taiwan-US drone partnership advanced, with Taiwan showcasing its capabilities at a major US drone exhibition. A European lithography ETF surpassed $150 million in assets under management, reflecting investor interest in the semiconductor sector. An easyJet flight from Egypt made an emergency landing in Rome due to a power bank incident. Market sentiment in the US reacted positively to expectations of peace talks.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>China's announced new mining controls and fast-tracking of strategic mineral reserves on May 22 signal potential future supply chain disruptions for critical minerals, intensifying resource nationalism and creating market uncertainty regarding resource access.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:** China announced on May 22 its intent to impose new mining controls and fast-track strategic mineral reserves. A Taiwan-US drone partnership was reported on May 21, with Taiwan participating in the largest US drone exhibition.

**Africa:** An easyJet flight carrying 180 passengers from Hurghada, Egypt, to London Luton was forced to make an emergency landing in Rome on May 19 due to a passenger's power bank.

**Europe:** An easyJet flight from Hurghada, Egypt, to London Luton was forced to make an emergency landing in Rome on May 19, diverting the aircraft to another destination due to a passenger's power bank.

**Americas:** On May 21, the Trump administration committed $2 billion to quantum computing firms, leading to a surge in related stocks. The largest US drone exhibition on May 21 featured a Taiwan pavilion, where a Taiwan-US drone partnership was noted to have potential business opportunities of $1.3 billion. Expectations for peace talks on May 22 led to a rise in the New York Stock Exchange.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Europe:** The Corgi Lithography & Semiconductor Photonics ETF (EUV) surpassed $150 million in assets under management within two weeks of its launch, as reported on May 21.
</LITHO>

</REE>

<MILITARY>

</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>The week of May 15-22 was marked by strategic investments in emerging technologies and intensifying efforts in resource control. The Trump administration's $2 billion commitment to quantum computing underscored a focus on advanced technological leadership and boosted related stocks. China's move to tighten control over strategic minerals points to an evolving landscape of resource nationalism and potential future supply chain shifts. The growth of the Corgi Lithography ETF highlights continued investor confidence in semiconductor manufacturing technology.
</CONCLUSION>
<INDIA></INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA></WEST_ASIA>
<FINAL_CONCLUSION>Looking forward, the global technology landscape will continue to be shaped by national strategic investments in advanced computing and semiconductor technologies, driven by competition for technological supremacy. China's proactive stance on critical mineral reserves signals an increased focus on supply chain resilience and resource leverage, which could influence international trade dynamics. Defense industrial cooperation, such as the Taiwan-US drone partnership, suggests ongoing efforts to bolster regional security capabilities. Market reactions indicate that investor confidence remains sensitive to geopolitical developments and expectations of diplomatic progress.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
